summary: Hyakudai Sakamoto (1928–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1964–1999), Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, and The Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and was attested in 2015 as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar born in 1964. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Virginia (2010). He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Madhav M. Deshpande (attested 2016).

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University (~1929–1932), and Jesus College, Oxford (~1932–1935), he taught at Bangor University (~1936–1955) and instructed Julius Lipner.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and has served as Professor and Principal Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Lancaster University. He taught at St Martin's College (~1986–2007) and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Cumbria (~2007–2014).

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and was a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute, Monash University, attested in 2005.
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford. He served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Professor at Aichi Bunkyo University in 2000.

Ian Reader is a religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Leeds. He held posts at Kansai Gaidai, Stirling, Lancaster, and Manchester, where he was Emeritus Professor (~2006–2015).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar in 2007. He serves as Associate Professor and Chairman of the Department of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959), where he later held an administrative post (~1974–2007), and taught William S. Waldron and Nobuchiyo Kotani.

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo, where he was professor emeritus (1965–1971). He also taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965).

Ichiro Katayama is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno. He served as assistant professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is attested in 2026 as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a sinologist and historian who studied under Jitsuzo Kuwabara at Kyoto University (~1922–1925). He later held a post at Kyoto University (~1936–1965) and taught Mamoru Tonami.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941). He was affiliated with the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali is an archaeology and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He was a professor at Peshawar, director of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's archaeology directorate, and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).
